subject: Deployment mode qualification & pricing follow-up (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Jenna Park <jenna.park@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Deployment mode qualification & next steps

Hi Jenna — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of requirements you shared:
- Latency target: 150–250ms p95 for 1–2k concurrent users per region
- Typical request size: ~400 tokens in/average response ~250 tokens out
- Peak QPS: ~40 sustained, bursts to ~120 for short windows
- Data residency: US only, PHI/limited PII (must go to private network or dedicated pool)
- Uptime / SLA expectation: enterprise SLA (99.9%+)

Initial deployment-mode thinking:
- Hosted API: fastest to ship, pay-as-you-go per-token; good for POC and early testing but harder to guarantee isolation/enterprise SLA without enterprise plans.
- Dedicated capacity: recommended if you need predictable throughput and strong isolation; cost via reserved commits (monthly/annual) with predictable unit economics for peak workloads.
- Private VPC / on-prem: required only if your security team insists on air-gapped/on-prem or very strict KMS/HSM controls — higher ops and infra cost.

Asks / action items for you:
1) Confirm expected average monthly active tokens (approx) and committed peak concurrency for sizing.
2) Confirm procurement timeline (you mentioned end of Q2?).
3) Please introduce Tom Liu (procurement) and any security contacts we should include for the checklist.

My next steps:
- I attached a lightweight cost model (redwood_cost_model_acmehealth_v1.xlsx) with two scenarios: hosted per-token projection vs dedicated reserved capacity (3-month and 12-month commit examples) and an initial SOW draft.
- Schedule a 30-min follow-up to walk through the model and reserve sizing. Proposed: Wed Mar 11 at 10:00 AM PT — does that work for you?

Thanks — happy to adjust the model once you confirm tokens/concurrency.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0147

Subject: Re: Deployment mode qualification & next steps

Hi Aditya — thanks for the summary, that matches what we discussed. A few clarifications: 
- We expect ~30M in tokens/month initially (QA + user-facing features), ramping to ~120M over 6–9 months if the pilot goes well.
- Sustained QPS of 30–50, with short bursts to ~120. Concurrency around 1.5–2k users concurrently during peak windows.
- Security: Must be in our VPC or a dedicated tenant; on-prem would be a last resort due to ops.
- Procurement: target decision by end of Q2 (June 30). Tom is our procurement lead — I’ve cc'd him. He'll coordinate contract review and T&Cs.

Can you include a quick split in the model showing: (A) hosted per-token cost at our volumes, (B) dedicated 6-month reserved vs 12-month reserved, with break-even points? Also include any one-time onboarding costs and estimated egress/backups if relevant.

Wed Mar 11 10AM PT works for a call. I'll loop in our security lead if needed after your model.

Thanks,
Jenna
Director of Product, Acme Health
jenna.park@acmehealth.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Tom Liu <tom.liu@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Deployment mode qualification & next steps — cost model attached

Hi Jenna / Tom — attached is the model and a short SOW draft. High-level summary from the spreadsheet: 

Hosted (per-token) — baseline scenario (30M tokens/month):
- Estimated cost: ~$1,200–1,800/month (per-token pricing tiered; includes inference + embeddings)
- Pros: no upfront commitment, flexible during ramp
- Cons: unit cost stabilizes at higher volumes; less control over isolation/SLA unless moved to enterprise tier

Dedicated (reserved capacity) — conservative 6-month commit for your peaks:
- Estimated cost (6-month reserved pool sized for sustained 50 QPS / burst up to 120): ~$45k/month committed capacity; effective unit cost (tokens) drops ~60–70% vs hosted at your peak volumes
- 12-month commit reduces monthly committed price by another ~10–15% and gives better unit economics if you expect steady usage
- Pros: predictable latency, stronger isolation, SLA options; recommended for production at scale
- Cons: higher upfront commitment and capacity planning required; unused headroom is paid for unless we add burst/auto-scale credits in contract

Private VPC / On-prem:
- Only recommend if compliance/security absolutely requires customer-managed network and HSM. Higher setup & recurring infra cost.

One-time/other costs:
- Onboarding & security review: estimated 8–12 engineering days (we show a one-time services estimate in the SOW draft)
- Optional: enhanced observability & extended retention add-ons: shown in model as optional line items

Next steps / proposed agenda for Wed Mar 11 10:00 AM PT:
1) Walk through the cost model assumptions & break-even analysis (10 min)
2) Sizing confirmation for reserved pool (10 min)
3) Procurement & timeline checkpoints + security contacts (10 min)

I’ve attached: redwood_cost_model_acmehealth_v1.xlsx (detailed tabs: assumptions, hosted vs dedicated, 6/12-month scenarios) and redwood_sow_draft_acmehealth_v1.pdf (onboarding + SLA options). Please open the model and we’ll iterate on the numbers during the call.

Call invite sent for Wed Mar 11 10:00 AM PT.

Best,
Aditya
